bull.b: A large, sticky retail deposit base ($144bn; 87% of funding; multi-year customer growth) supplies low-cost, durable funding. That reduces reliance on volatile wholesale markets, supports sustained asset growth (loans/leases), and underpins net interest income and funding resilience over cycles.

Strong, repeatable origination scale (retail originations +21% YoY; record applications) and growing corporate finance assets demonstrate diversified, high-return growth engines. Durable dealer/distribution relationships and scale support sustained loan production and fee income across market cycles.

Management's upper‑3s NIM target alongside a CET1 ratio near 10.1% signals improving earning power with a meaningful capital buffer. Tighter loss guidance and modest buybacks/dividends indicate disciplined capital allocation that can sustain returns while preserving regulatory and balance sheet flexibility.

bear.b: Persistently elevated leverage (D/E ~1.4–1.6) reduces financial flexibility and amplifies earnings sensitivity to credit or margin shocks. Higher leverage limits the firm's ability to absorb losses or pursue opportunistic investments without raising external capital during stress periods.

Despite solid operating cash flow (~$4.6B TTM), very thin and volatile free cash flow constrains internal funding for buybacks, dividends or inorganic growth. Limited cash conversion increases reliance on capital markets for strategic actions and weakens shock absorption over multiple quarters.

Material CECL reserve builds and a sizable provision increase highlight sensitivity of earnings to credit assumptions amid rapid asset growth. Combined with 30+ day delinquencies still elevated, reserve volatility can swing earnings and capital needs, forcing defensive actions or margin trade-offs.
